Server molecule packs

Add molecules to a server by installing a folder or ZIP in its pack directory. Each pack contains pack.mcmeta and molecule JSON files; the examples bind water to an existing bucket and create an ethanol sample item.

Install a pack

Pack installation locations
Location Scope
config/avogadro/packs/ Every world on this Minecraft instance or dedicated server.
<world>/avogadro/packs/ Only that world; overrides instance packs.

Each direct child folder or .zip is a pack. ZIPs must contain pack.mcmeta directly at their root, without an extra enclosing folder. Rename a folder or archive so its name ends in .disabled to disable it. Other loose files are ignored. 

chemistry.zip
  pack.mcmeta
  data/example/molecules/water.json
  data/example/molecules/samples/ethanol.json
  data/example/tags/items/bottles.json
  data/example/tags/fluids/solvents.json
  assets/...                         (optional client resources)

Describe the pack in pack.mcmeta

{
  "pack": {
    "pack_format": 3,
    "description": "Chemistry models and sample items"
  }
}

Avogadro supports pack_format 3, the Minecraft 1.12.2 resource-pack format, and requires a string description.

Bind water to an existing bucket and fluid

Save this as data/example/molecules/water.json. The path supplies the ID example:water. 

{
  "name": "Water",
  "atoms": [
    {
        "e": "O",
        "x": 0,
        "y": 0,
        "z": 0
    },
    {
        "e": "H",
        "x": 0.7586,
        "y": 0.5043,
        "z": 0
    },
    {
        "e": "H",
        "x": -0.7586,
        "y": 0.5043,
        "z": 0
    }
  ],
  "bonds": [[0, 1], [0, 2]],
  "items": ["minecraft:water_bucket"],
  "fluids": ["water"],
  "match_containers": true,
  "generate_item": false
}
Associations in a molecule definition
Field Meaning
smiles The existing SMILES parser builds schematic geometry, including implicit hydrogens.
items / fluids Existing item or fluid selectors. Metadata and partial NBT matching use the ordinary association rules.
item_tags / fluid_tags References to Avogadro binding dictionaries under data/<namespace>/tags/items/ and tags/fluids/; these do not create new Minecraft registry entries.
match_containers Allows matching a filled container through its fluid contents.

For a binding dictionary such as data/example/tags/items/bottles.json, use {"values":["minecraft:glass_bottle"]}. Later tag files append by default; "replace":true replaces the earlier list. See precise matching and the complete field reference.

Create an ethanol sample item

Save this as data/example/molecules/samples/ethanol.json.

{
  "name": "Ethanol",
  "smiles": "CCO",
  "generate_item": true
}

This adds a molecule sample variant identified as example:samples/ethanol. The underlying item is avogadro:molecule, with the stable molecule ID in its avogadro_molecule NBT string. It does not register an item named example:ethanol or add a crafting recipe. Existing saved samples retain their ID when pack ordering changes.

The complete molecule schema is supported: explicit atoms/bonds, structures and edits, copies, assemblies, polymers, networks, crystals, isotopes and atomic configurations. Copy sources resolve against the combined server definitions, including other packs.

Choose which pack wins and reload your changes

Within each pack directory, names sort by case-sensitive filename in ascending order; later names win. Resources inside a pack sort by path. Use names such as 01-base and 02-overrides.zip to make priority obvious.

  1. Mod resources and generated reference defaults
  2. Java registrations
  3. Instance molecule packs
  4. Instance JSON under config/avogadro/server/data/
  5. World molecule packs
  6. World JSON under <world>/avogadro/data/
  7. Script registrations

Packs load on server startup. After editing, installing, removing or disabling one, run /avogadro reload with permission level 2. Clients already connected receive additions, replacements and removals through Avogadro's normal snapshot synchronization; later joins receive the current snapshot. Removing a pack reveals lower-priority definitions.

An unreadable or invalid enabled pack rejects the reload and retains the previous complete snapshot. Errors identify the pack and, for resource reads, the entry. Pack definitions are validated even when another source overrides them. Existing non-pack loading retains its earlier tolerant behavior. On an initial startup without a successful snapshot, a rejected load leaves the server molecule view empty and logs the reason.

Install molecule data and textures on the correct side

Installing the pack on the server loads only its supported data/ JSON. It never enables, sends or distributes assets/. To use the same archive as a client resource pack, install and select it through Minecraft's resource-pack menu or configure the server's ordinary resource-pack distribution separately.

A player's selected resource packs can change their local molecule presentation; they cannot register authoritative server data. Server molecule packs are installed by the server owner. Both ends still require compatible Avogadro builds.

Set defaults and make exceptions for selected molecules

Use one settings file to hide a collection from HEI, remove its generated samples from creative tabs, or turn off its tooltip and world-HUD previews. Definitions, saved items, bindings and copy references remain available. These settings do not change personal themes or enable previews that a player has disabled locally.

Put avogadro-settings.json at the root of a pack, beside pack.mcmeta. Server owners can override pack choices in config/avogadro/pack-settings.json; a world can override those choices in <world>/avogadro/pack-settings.json. 

{
  "defaults": {
    "hei_visible": false,
    "creative_visible": false
  },
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "Show common chemistry",
      "match": {
          "molecule_tags": ["example:common"]
      },
      "exclude": {
          "ids": ["example:experimental_sample"]
      },
      "set": {
          "hei_visible": true,
          "creative_visible": true
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Start polymer viewers with twelve units",
      "match": {
          "classifications": ["polymer"]
      },
      "set": {
          "polymer_preview_units": 12
      }
    }
  ]
}

This example hides samples by default, then shows molecules carrying the example:common molecule tag, except for the named experimental sample. Add "molecule_tags": ["example:common"] to a molecule JSON file to put it in that group. These tags describe molecules; they are separate from item and fluid binding tags. Tags are local to each definition and are not inherited through copy.

Available settings
Setting Default Effect
hei_visible true Lists the molecule card and its generated sample in HEI.
creative_visible true Lists generated samples in creative tabs. Existing samples still resolve.
tooltips true Allows automatic molecule previews in item and fluid tooltips.
world_hud true Allows molecule previews in supported world HUDs.
polymer_preview_units 0 Initial repeat count when opening a linear-polymer viewer. Zero uses the authored count; 1–64 requests a count, limited further by that polymer's atom/bond limits. Networks and stored template geometry are unchanged.

A rule can match ids, namespaces, classifications or molecule_tags. Each is a nonempty array. Values within an array are alternatives; when several selector fields are supplied, all fields must match. Classifications are element, molecule, crystal, polymer and mixture, using the resolved classification. exclude uses the same selectors. An omitted or empty match matches everything; an explicit empty exclude excludes everything.

Settings apply in this order: definition-local presentation values (or built-in defaults), instance pack files, world pack files, the instance settings file, then the world settings file. Pack files follow the same filename ordering as their definitions. Each settings file applies its defaults first and its rules in array order. The last matching assignment wins for that setting; selectors have no hidden specificity ranking. Pack defaults apply to the complete collection, so use a namespace match when a rule should affect only your pack's molecules.

Invalid settings reject a reload even if the offending rule matches nothing. Use the server commands to reload, check the combined collection, or inspect an installed molecule's settings.

Check the combined collection before sharing it

Check the collection on your authoring server before distributing packs; individual pack sizes do not establish that the combination fits.

The complete selected snapshot must fit 8 MiB before and after compression, with at most 8,192 entries in each molecule/item-tag/fluid-tag map. A small ZIP can still exceed the uncompressed limit. Overrides, UTF-8 text, identifiers, length prefixes and effective display settings all count. Check packs together: passing individual checks does not establish that their combination fits.

Java authoring tools can call MoleculePacks.check(List<Path> directories, MoleculeResources.Data base) without installing definitions. Supply pack root directories in priority order and external definitions/tags in base. The returned MoleculeSync.Budget provides fits(), summary(), both byte counts and all measured limit problems. Invalid pack content throws IOException. This check covers those supplied inputs; the server command also includes the actual world's installed registrations and overrides.

Display settings require synchronization protocol 6. Update Avogadro on both client and server together; older protocols are rejected rather than silently ignoring visibility rules.

Keep packs within the supported limits

Each JSON or metadata file is limited to 256 KiB. A pack may contain at most 16,384 entries, 64 path levels and 32 MiB of supported data JSON. Each pack directory permits at most 128 enabled packs and 64 MiB of supported data JSON. Existing molecule geometry and synchronized snapshot limits still apply. Symbolic links, duplicate ZIP entry names, absolute paths and traversal paths are rejected. ZIPs are read directly without extraction.

Recover safely from interrupted distribution

Version 1.1.0 uses protocol 6; install matching client and server versions. Partial transfers expire after 30 seconds without a chunk. Failed reload delivery disconnects the affected client with a reconnect message. Disconnect invalidates decoded-but-queued snapshots. Missing optional item/fluid tags report bounded warnings and remain legal. Resolved association lists allow 1024 entries each and an 8 MiB combined accounting budget, in addition to synchronization byte limits.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or setting Arguments What it does
pack.mcmeta pack_format; description Use pack_format 3 and a string description. Put this file directly at a ZIP’s root.
data/namespace/molecules/path.json Namespace and file path The example path data/example/molecules/water.json defines example:water.
Tag JSON values / replace Selector list; replacement flag Append tag entries by default or replace the earlier list explicitly.
/avogadro reload Server command; permission level 2 Reload common server sources and synchronize connected clients.

When you finish: Pack loading owns its file access. To disable a pack, rename its folder or ZIP with the .disabled suffix and reload. A rejected pack reload keeps the previous complete result; fix the reported file before retrying.
